approach: Make the two late disk gates (before the checks, before the verifier) hold the job instead of closing it failed. A new `Athena::hold_for_disk` (in run/close.rs, beside the closing code) pushes the attempt's records through a new shared `push_closing_records` (extracted from `close_dispatched`), commits them with no Score and no Outcome, writes the hold marker (free and required amounts), keeps the resume mark, removes the verifier snapshot, and returns `Err(LowDisk)`. The job stays `Dispatched` (it reads as interrupted), so no failure, no introspection, no failure class, no scope-guard attempt. The drain already maps `LowDisk` to `RunStep::Held` and an interrupted job is already worked by the drain's internal retry, which resumes the kept candidate via `resume_seed` with no planner or producer run. So the hold costs no drain attempt, and a later pass resumes it. Status and display show the hold for an interrupted job. Then rewrite the stale scope_guard test, rewrite the drain/run tests that asserted the old Failed path, reword the docs/decisions.md entry so no supersession phrase lacks a target id, update the module docs, and add a CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Leave a held job Dispatched with committed attempt records and no Outcome/Score; reuse the existing interrupted-job resume (drain's internal retry plus resume_seed) rather than a new resume path in go_job.
decisions.reason: resumable_stop already treats a Dispatched job with no process as resumable, steward::interrupted_work already lists it for a drain, and scope_guard::attempt_of returns None for a job with no closed state, so it counts as neither an attempt nor a work failure. The producer's cost stays recorded because the invocations are committed.

rejected.option: Keep closing the job Failed with an environment reason and rely on `athena retry`
rejected.why: This is the behavior the request removes; a full-disk drain would still end a job failed.

rejected.option: Resume the same job id inside go_job
rejected.why: dispatch() builds the whole run context (prediction commit, job record, config pin) and would need a second entry. The retry path already does this safely and keeps the reading, the base check and the 'only records/ changed' guard.

decisions.choice: Turn a verifier write-probe failure into a LowDisk hold too (measured free bytes, the configured requirement), and print the probe error as a ui line.
decisions.reason: The hold needs one type that drain, status and the marker already understand. A workspace that cannot be written is the same cause as a full disk, and criterion 7 forbids a retry-telling failure on this path.

rejected.option: Keep the probe failure as a retry-telling failure
rejected.why: It leaves a path that fails a job for the environment and violates criterion 7.

rejected.option: Add a reason string to LowDisk
rejected.why: LowDisk is Copy and is serialized in hold markers; changing it is more than this job needs.

decisions.reason: One list of what an attempt commits (invocations, plans, critiques, baseline, candidate, verification) stops the held and the closed paths drifting apart.

rejected.option: Copy the push loop into hold_for_disk

decisions.choice: Clear the old job's hold marker and resume mark when a retry consumes it (settle_resume_marks), and leave the cleanup of the held job's target to the existing idle sweep.
decisions.reason: The sweep already removes build directories of unlocked jobs; the hold must not free space itself except the verifier snapshot, since the resume needs only the committed candidate.

rejected.option: Close the held job as superseded when the retry lands
rejected.why: Out of scope; interrupted jobs are left as they are today.

decisions.choice: Reword the docs/decisions.md entry so it names no supersession without a target decision id (or uses no such phrase).
decisions.reason: The backtest (crates/athena-cli/src/backtest.rs, line ~337) flags 'supersession phrases without a target id'; the last candidate's entry did.

rejected.option: Edit the backtest or its confirmed list
rejected.why: The entry is the fault, and the backtest is a guard that should stay as it is.

risks.risk: Returning Err from check_and_verify bypasses close_dispatched, so job-level cleanup (clean_job, kept timed-out work, stage rows) is skipped, leaving build directories and the verifier snapshot on a full disk.
risks.mitigation: hold_for_disk removes the verifier snapshot (as the old failure path did) and does not call clean_job. The next gate's sweep_idle_targets removes the idle build directory (the held job is unlocked). A test checks the order in the output.

risks.risk: A resumed job (retry of a held job) that holds again leaves a chain of Dispatched jobs.
risks.mitigation: hold_for_disk drops the consumed job's resume and hold marks, and the new job writes its own resume mark. A drain test runs three passes and checks a bounded set of jobs.

risks.risk: Other tests or code read the old Failed behavior (introspection tests, `retry.rs`, `is_environment_reason` consumers, Verdict::Environment tests).
risks.mitigation: `is_environment_reason`, `resumable_stop` and Verdict::Environment stay for old failed jobs and for check-timeout. A workspace-wide `cargo test --locked` is the check; the grep in cli tests found no other low-disk assertions beyond drain.rs and binary.rs.

risks.risk: The scope-guard 'resumed' read relies on the held job being Dispatched with no producer in the retry.
risks.mitigation: `resumed_candidate` already accepts a Dispatched target via `resumable_stop`; the rewritten test asserts `resumed` and Accepted.

demonstrations.method: New drain test `low_disk_after_the_build_holds_the_job_and_does_not_fail_it`. It builds a disk_fixture with the real steps, wrapping `rated_scenario().script()` so the producer call writes the `simulated_free` file with 3 GB (the pattern of `go_with_disk`). It runs `drain::drain(&steps, work_everything(), &Quiet)` once. A second variant sets free space to 3 GB once `jobs/<id>/verify` exists (`low_once_verifying`), for the hold before the verifier.
demonstrations.observes: The job report shows outcome `environment: low disk` and text with `3.0 GB` and `10.0 GB`; `failed_item` is None; the job is `JobState::Dispatched` with `outcome` None and `verification` None; there is no Verifier invocation and no Score or Outcome record; no `athena retry` appears in lines or reason; the hold marker holds the amounts.
demonstrations.fails_without: Before the change the same run finishes `OutcomeState::Failed` with a reason that contains `athena retry <job>`, so the Dispatched, no-Outcome and no-retry-text assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `drain::drain` over `real_steps(&athena, &lander)`; fake: the scripted driver `Scenario` and a free-space function injected with `athena.state.with_free_space(simulated_free)`; both exist today (drain.rs tests, around lines 1498, 1766 and 1673).

demonstrations.method: New test in the same file that continues the held state: raise free space with `set_free(&athena, 500_000_000_000)`, run a second `drain::drain`, and count producer calls through the script wrapper.
demonstrations.observes: The second drain finishes with the job landed (RecordingLander holds the job). The producer invocation count is unchanged from the first pass, there is no planner call, and no `athena retry` command ran (the test calls only drain). The resume line `resume     job <id> kept its candidate` is in the output. The held job's hold marker is gone.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the hold, the job is closed Failed and the drain's second pass does not resume it. With a hold but no resume, the producer count rises or the job never lands.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::drain` with `RealSteps` (it calls `athena.retry` internally for an interrupted job), the producer-counting `Script` wrapper, `set_free`; all exist today.

demonstrations.method: New test: after the first held pass, run two more drains with free space still 3 GB. Free space comes from the same `simulated_free` seam.
demonstrations.observes: Each pass reports the item `environment: low disk` with `failed_item` None, `landed` 0, and `Stop` not `RepeatedFailure`; the held job's records are unchanged between passes (no Outcome, no Score, no new producer invocation); the item is attempted once per pass, with no second attempt in the report.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a hold counted as a failed attempt, the drain would retry in the same pass (jobs.len() 2) or end with `Stop::RepeatedFailure`.
demonstrations.seam: `drain::drain` over real steps with `set_free`; exists today.

open_questions: Does binary.rs's harness let a test share the repo and state directory between an in-process Athena and a spawned `athena status`? If not, the hold must be made with `disk::write_hold` on a dispatched fixture job. ATHENA_FREE_BYTES is constant for a process, so it cannot make a mid-run drop.

The brief's 'no `athena retry`' is read as no person running the CLI command. The drain's own interrupted-job path calls `Athena::retry` internally (a new job; the reader runs once). I did not read steward::interrupted_work in full to confirm that it lists a held job whose process is gone.
The held job stays Dispatched (shown as interrupted) after a retry resumes it, as any interrupted job does today; a drain does not list it again once a retry names it. Closing it is not planned.
I did not read the exact rule in backtest.rs (~line 337) or the failing decisions.md entry; the producer must read both and run the backtest test before writing the entry.
The new hold commits the replay record when the hold is before the verifier. This is harmless, but it was not checked whether a resumed job writes a second replay record.
